# Remedy

Remedy turns recall-photo reviews into traceable PayPal refunds. Owners submit destruction photographs with a one-time code. AI describes the evidence, fixed rules decide whether a claim passes or needs review, and PayPal Payouts sends eligible refunds.

## Product

For companies running CPSC refund recalls, particularly smaller sellers who receive destruction photos by email. Owners need clear instructions and a short refund path. Companies need evidence review, human decisions for uncertainty, payout tracking and recall reporting.

The owner reviews the recall, logs in with PayPal, writes an issued code, and photographs the product according to the recall instructions. The code/session lasts ten minutes. Desktop users can continue on a phone through QR handoff. Real claims use a camera interface; the judge demo uses clearly labeled prepared photos.

## Five checks

1. Photos arrived within the claim's ten-minute session carrying its key.
2. Photo fingerprints do not match an earlier claim within the configured threshold.
3. One open or paid claim per verified PayPal account on the recall.
4. The model reads the label/code; code compares the text.
5. The model describes whether required destruction evidence is visible.

The first three run before AI. Fixed rules reject a no, hold an unclear answer for human review, and pass otherwise. Auto-pay and duplicate/account checks remain in code. Payment status distinguishes sent/settling from confirmed. Failures and uncertainty are held; eligible rejected claims can request review once.

## Company tools

AG Grid queue with status tabs, filters/search, sorting, grouping, selection, CSV, keyboard navigation and mobile cards. The evidence drawer shows deciding reason, checks, model quotations, photographs and payout timeline. AG Studio Insights provides custom widgets, charts and a Recall analyst. The analyst can read, explain, chart and draft; it cannot approve or pay. CPSC notice import drafts editable requirements for human review before publishing. Settings, claim links/QR and printable progress reports complete the workflow.

## What is real, sandbox and illustrative

The judge flow uses real model/PayPal sandbox calls with prepared photos. Genuine and wrong-code cases reach AI; outside-session and reused-photo cases stop in the pre-checks.

All money in this build is PayPal sandbox money from Remedy's one shared sandbox business account. Per-company funding requires future PayPal partner onboarding. Kikea Store is the firm named in the public example recall, not a Remedy customer. The $29.99 amount is a demo setting.

The homepage walkthrough and seven built-in company claims are illustrative. Some carry real recorded model answers, but generated payer IDs, shifting sample dates and stand-in payout records. RM-0442's 15-second send and 55-second confirmation are illustrative, not fresh provider calls. Fresh judge claims appear beside these only to the browser round that created them.

## Limitations

The model does not reliably detect generated images. Two clean generated images with the correct code passed the 9 November photo-check evaluation in all six runs. The session proves admission with its key and timing, not camera provenance. Real phone handwriting remains untested in that evaluation. A 64-bit dHash check catches the documented tested edits; mirrors and larger crops can evade it. Model-call cost/timing is not end-to-end operating cost, customer pricing or a settlement guarantee. See README for full dataset scope and limitations.

## Architecture and links

Next.js, React, TypeScript on Vercel; PayPal identity/Payouts/status/verified webhooks; OpenAI structured vision; Vercel Blob or local storage; AG Grid/Studio; public CPSC data.
